claims.text: No single accepted approach: many clinicians treat young, otherwise healthy women with classic dysuria, frequency and urgency and no red flags without any testing.
claims.quote: Many clinicians presumptively give antibiotics for cystitis without any testing (sometimes not even urinalysis) in young, otherwise healthy women presenting with classic dysuria, frequency, and urgency and without red flag findings.

claims.text: Urinalysis and culture of a clean-catch midstream sample; culture is recommended with risk factors for multidrug-resistant infection.
claims.quote: Others evaluate everyone with a clean-catch midstream urine sample for urinalysis and culture. Urine culture is recommended in patients with risk factors for multidrug-resistant infections.

claims.text: Pregnancy test in women of childbearing age.
claims.quote: In women of childbearing age, a pregnancy test is done

claims.text: Wet mount if there is vaginal discharge.
claims.quote: Vaginal discharge warrants a wet mount.

claims.text: Gonorrhea and chlamydia testing (culture or PCR) of cervical or urethral samples, because many infected patients present atypically.
claims.quote: Many clinicians routinely obtain samples of cervical (women) or urethral (men) exudate for STI testing (gonococcus and chlamydia culture or polymerase chain reaction [PCR]) because many infected patients do not have a typical presentation.

claims.text: Culture count: more than 10^5 colony-forming units/mL suggests infection; in symptomatic patients, counts as low as 10^2 or 10^3 can indicate UTI.
claims.quote: A finding of > 10 5 bacteria colony-forming units (CFU)/mL suggests infection . In symptomatic patients, sometimes counts as low as 10 2 or 10 3 CFUs indicate UTI.

claims.text: Cystoscopy and urinary tract imaging if there is no response to antibiotics, symptoms recur, or there is hematuria without infection.
claims.quote: Cystoscopy and imaging of the urinary tract may be indicated to check for obstruction, anatomic abnormalities, cancer, or other problems in patients who have no response to antibiotics, recurrent symptoms, or hematuria without infection.
